name: manual_979234
claim: GitHub stacked PRs: a stack is a chain where each PR's base is the branch of the PR below it and the bottom targets trunk; it needs a fully linear history and merges bottom-up. 'Merge conflicts' on a stacked PR usually means trunk moved (here, another PR landed the same fix). Fix it with a cascading rebase from the bottom (gh stack rebase, resolve, git add, gh stack rebase --continue, gh stack push), not the server-side 'Rebase stack' button, which cannot resolve textual conflicts and creates unsigned commits. Without the gh-stack extension, do the same with git rebase --onto <new-lower-tip> <old-base> per branch and a lease-pinned push naming the ref and its expected SHA. A bare number in gh stack checkout is a stack number; stack and PR numbers share one namespace. Re-seat upper layers whenever a lower layer changes, and if a safety hook blocks the push, verify locally and hand the operator the exact lease-pinned command rather than routing around the hook.

decisions.notes: oramasys stack #64 = main <- #63 <- #62 (docs via gh.io/stacks and gh.io/stacks-resolving-conflicts, read with Firecrawl and Exa and cross-checked, 2026-10-18). #62 showed CONFLICTING because main had gained PR #22's own ruff-cleanup commit. A cascading rebase onto the server-rebased #63 resolved two conflicts; the operator then ran the lease-pinned push (319d447 -> da580b9) and both PRs showed MERGEABLE and CLEAN. When #63 later gained two commits, #62 had to be re-seated onto the new tip before that push, so confirm lower layers are final before pushing upper ones.
